what: boundary flips and last-position logit drift of an incremental prompt read vs a cold one-shot read
findings: The flip rate does not scale with the number of window seams: 7 seams gives 5 flips, 1 seam gives 5. Flips are float accumulation in the recurrent state, not an artefact of splitting the read.

Windowed prefill flips no more often than the warm-continuation path already in production at every window size tested (4-5 vs 5-6 samples of 24), and its logit drift is the same magnitude or smaller.

About 5 flips per 15,000 chunks, i.e. one boundary in ~3,000. The signed zero-flip bar is not met by windowing - and is not met by the read path already shipping either. No incremental read achieves it.
